cards.title: PTA Interpretation and Regulatory Thresholds
cards.claim: A PTA of 90% is a common benchmark for PK/PD cutoff determination but is not a universal scientific or clinical sufficiency threshold. A PTA <90% may be acceptable if the dose required for >90% PTA is poorly tolerated, or if the infection type is less severe and few organisms have MICs at the upper end of the range. Sponsors must justify the acceptability of PTA <90% based on clinical context.
conditions: Applicable when interpreting PTA results for dose regimen selection or breakpoint setting.
Requires justification for deviating from the 90% benchmark.
Depends on the severity of infection and spontaneous resolution rates.
required_inputs: Calculated PTA values for relevant MICs.
Clinical context regarding infection severity and pathogen burden.
Tolerability data for doses required to achieve higher PTAs.
limitations: PTA is a simulation output, not a direct clinical outcome.
Clinical exposure-response (E-R) relationships are often difficult to establish due to confounding factors (host immunity, adjunctive treatments).
90% is a guideline suggestion, not an absolute biological law.
cards.downstream_use: Inform regulatory submissions and dose selection discussions by justifying the chosen PTA threshold or explaining why a lower PTA is clinically acceptable.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Per-MIC PTA definition: exposure distribution, target, basis and window

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
